chapters.1.meaning: The messenger says he killed Saul. First Samuel 31 says Saul fell on his own sword.
chapters.2.meaning: David and Ishbosheth rule different parts of Israel. A contest between their men grows into a deadly battle.
chapters.2.lds: Why does Abner ask Joab to stop the fighting?
chapters.3.lds: What happens to Michal and her husband when David demands her return?
chapters.4.lds: Why does David punish men who expect a reward for killing his rival?
chapters.6.meaning: David celebrates the ark’s arrival but also fears its power. His dispute with Michal divides their household.
chapters.7.summary: David plans a house for God. God instead promises David a lasting royal family. David’s son will build the temple.
chapters.7.meaning: House can mean a building or a family. God’s promise links David’s family with Israel’s future.
chapters.8.lds: How does David’s growing rule affect the people his armies defeat?
chapters.10.meaning: David sends comfort after a king’s death. Hanun suspects a trick and shames the messengers. War follows.
chapters.10.lds: How could Hanun have tested his advisers’ claim before acting?
chapters.12.meaning: Nathan exposes David’s abuse of power. The child’s death also brings suffering to the household.
chapters.12.lds: The older manual compares verse 13 with the Joseph Smith Translation. That version changes Nathan’s words about David’s sin.
chapters.13.lds: What does Tamar ask Amnon to do? Who fails to protect her?
chapters.14.lds: How does Joab use the woman’s story to change David’s decision?
chapters.15.lds: How does Absalom use promises of justice to win support?
chapters.16.lds: Whose account does David hear before giving Ziba the land?
chapters.17.lds: Which people bring food and other help to David’s group?
chapters.18.lds: Why does David’s grief differ from his soldiers’ joy over victory?
chapters.19.meaning: Mephibosheth says Ziba deceived David. David divides the land without settling which account is true.
chapters.19.lds: Which disputes remain after David returns to rule?
chapters.22.lds: How does David’s song compare with his choices elsewhere in the book?
chapters.23.lds: How do the warriors’ actions show the risks of serving a king?
chapters.24.meaning: David asks why others suffer for his wrong. Samuel says God prompted the count. Chronicles names Satan instead.
people.ishbosheth.meaning: Ishbosheth depends on Abner’s support. When Abner leaves him, his rule soon ends in murder.
people.ahio.meaning: Ahio walks ahead of the cart that carries the ark.
people.benaiah.meaning: Benaiah’s courage wins him a place over David’s guards. The chapter recalls his battles with lions and soldiers.
people.ziba.meaning: Ziba gains land after accusing Mephibosheth. Mephibosheth later disputes his account.
people.machir.role: Host who shelters Mephibosheth and helps David
people.unnamed-infant.meaning: The child becomes ill after Nathan confronts David. David fasts and prays before the child dies.
people.abigail-sister.meaning: This Abigail is Amasa’s mother. She differs from the Abigail who marries David.
people.sibbecai.meaning: Sibbecai kills the Philistine warrior Saph at Gob.
people.josheb-basshebeth.meaning: The warrior list credits him with killing eight hundred men in one battle.
people.saul.meaning: Saul’s death divides Israel’s leadership. David mourns him instead of celebrating the loss of a rival.
people.nahash.meaning: David sends messengers to comfort Nahash’s son Hanun after Nahash dies.
people.jonathan-saul.meaning: David remembers Jonathan’s friendship. He later cares for Jonathan’s son Mephibosheth.
people.merab.meaning: Merab’s sons appear in the account of Saul’s family. Some old copies name Michal instead.
people.david.meaning: David makes Jerusalem his capital and helps Jonathan’s son. His abuse of power also harms Uriah and his own family.
places.jerusalem.summary: David makes Jerusalem his capital. The ark comes here, and his family rules from the city.
places.hebron.summary: Judah first crowns David at Hebron. He rules here before moving to Jerusalem.
places.mahanaim.summary: Ishbosheth rules from Mahanaim. David later shelters here while fleeing Absalom.
places.gibeon.summary: Abner’s and Joab’s men meet by Gibeon’s pool. Their contest becomes a battle.
places.bahurim.summary: Michal’s husband follows her as far as Bahurim. Shimei later curses David near this town.
places.tyre.summary: Tyre is Hiram’s coastal city. He sends workers and wood for David’s house.
places.rephaim.summary: The Philistines gather in the valley of Rephaim before fighting David.
places.gezer.summary: David pursues the Philistines toward Gezer after a battle near Jerusalem.
places.aram.summary: Aram includes Syrian groups that fight David’s forces. This marker shows a broad region.
places.hamath.summary: Hamath is Tou’s kingdom. He sends gifts after David defeats Hadadezer.
places.edom.summary: David’s forces defeat Edom and place guards there. The Edomites become subject to his rule.
places.lodebar.summary: Machir shelters Mephibosheth at Lo Debar before David calls him to Jerusalem.
places.rabbah.summary: Rabbah is the Ammonite royal city. Joab attacks it while David stays in Jerusalem.
places.jericho.summary: David’s shamed messengers wait at Jericho until their beards grow back.
places.thebez.summary: Joab recalls a woman killing Abimelech at Thebez. He expects David to remember this earlier battle.
places.baal-hazor.summary: Absalom holds a sheep-shearing feast at Baal Hazor. His servants kill Amnon there.
places.geshur.summary: Absalom flees to Geshur after Amnon’s death. His mother comes from its royal family.
places.tekoa.summary: Joab brings a woman from Tekoa to speak to David about Absalom.
places.kidron.summary: David crosses the Kidron valley while fleeing Jerusalem.
places.olives.summary: David climbs the Mount of Olives in grief while fleeing Absalom.
places.en-rogel.summary: Jonathan and Ahimaaz wait at En Rogel for news to carry to David.
places.jordan.summary: The Jordan separates David’s retreat from Jerusalem. His party crosses it to reach safety.
places.rogellim.summary: Barzillai comes from Rogelim. He provides food for David’s party.
places.gilead.summary: Gilead lies east of the Jordan. David receives help from people in this region.
places.gilgal.summary: Judah meets David at Gilgal when he returns after Absalom’s defeat.
places.abel.summary: Joab attacks Abel Beth Maacah while pursuing Sheba. A wise woman saves the town.
places.zela.summary: David arranges the burial of Saul and Jonathan at Zela in their family tomb.
places.dan.summary: Joab’s counting party travels to Dan near Israel’s northern limit.
places.sidon.summary: Joab’s counting party reaches the area toward Sidon during its long journey.
